content: Tongue diseases can either be congenital (present from birth) or acquired later in life. The condition of the tongue often provides valuable diagnostic information about various systemic or localized medical conditions. For example, the appearance of a strawberry tongue can be indicative of certain underlying diseases. Historically, the examination of the tongue has been an essential component of a thorough medical evaluation. Examples of tongue conditions include: White tongue: The presence of white spots, patches, or a coating on the tongue can be a symptom of several medical conditions, such as: Side effects of antibiotics Oral candidiasis (a fungal infection caused by Candida species) Dehydration Leukoplakia (a condition characterized by white patches on the mucous membranes) Keratosis pharyngis (a rare condition involving keratinization of the pharyngeal mucosa) Jaundice (which can also cause a yellow discoloration of the tongue) Yellow tongue: This can occur as a result of jaundice or other conditions affecting the liver or bile metabolism. Lie bumps: These are small, raised dots that typically appear on the tip of the tongue. They may be associated with irritation, minor trauma, or other factors. Glossitis: This refers to inflammation of the tongue, which can result in swelling, redness, and changes in texture. Hypoglossia: A congenital condition characterized by an abnormally short tongue. Macroglossia: A condition where the tongue is abnormally large, which can be congenital or acquired. In traditional Chinese medicine, the tongue is carefully examined and observed as part of the diagnostic process. The appearance, texture, and color of the tongue are believed to reflect the state of internal organs and overall health.
